parsed.explanation: The quote is verbatim from §3, and the only fact preceding it is that V contains at most one positive number; the text never establishes g ≥ 0. §1 only notes g(x) > −x, which permits negative values, and no later section excludes them — §4–§6 and Lemma 1 all presuppose V ⊆ {0, c}. So the dichotomy (i)/(ii) does not follow: a priori V could contain a negative value d. The objection's repair is mathematically correct: by (4), g(x + nd) = d for all n, and each x + nd = fⁿ(x) must lie in R_{>0}; if d < 0 this fails for large n, so d ≥ 0. Since this two-line exclusion appears nowhere, the necessity argument rests on an unjustified dichotomy and is incomplete as written; the obligation (N) is thus not fully discharged.
